locator.text: Display 27.6, p. 27, in the proof of Proposition 4.2

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Both components are stated, with the same constants, exponents and signs; the rewriting is only in how the first component is written and in which realisation of the leading field carries it. (i) leading_shear_eq_profile is about the leading fields F = leadingFrequency = q^{-A-1/2} phi_0 / C and G = leadingAxial = q^{-A} U_0, which are u_theta / r and u_z of (4.3) (leadingFrequency keeps the 1/R factor, so it is the angular frequency, not u_theta). (ii) Its left side is shearVector = (R * d_R F, d_R G). The second entry is d_r u_z verbatim. The first entry is r d_r(u_theta/r), which equals d_r u_theta - u_theta/r by the product rule; the Lean never forms d_r u_theta itself, because u_theta/r is the regular object across the axis. (iii) Its right side is leadingFrequency(p) • (-angularShear, -signedAxialShear) = (-q^{-A-1/2} F a, +q^{-A-1/2} F b_s), since angularShear E = 1 - 2 X E_X / E is the a of (4.11) verbatim and signedAxialShear E U = -(2 X U_X / E) is -b_s verbatim, matching the paper's s = (a, -b_s); leadingFrequency_eq supplies the prefactor q^{-A-1/2} F. (iv) Caveat on the carrier: the theorem is stated for the chart/coefficient-defined leading fields of BaseChartJets under hypotheses that d.phi 0 = C * P.f and d.axial 0 = P.U as radial germs at the point, not for LeadingStress.physicalVelocity, which is the field used in the Lean counterpart of Proposition 4.2; I found no declaration giving this shear identity directly for LeadingStress.swirlProfile / axialProfile.
